Class Row

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.layout.Row
public final class Row extends Object
Build-time horizontal layout helper. Computes per-child childX positions for a sequence of ElementSpecs under uniform spacing and a cross-axis alignment policy. Emits a flat list of positioned PanelElements to the consumer.

Row exists only during the .build() call chain. After build() returns, the Row builder discharges its job and is dead; no Row reference should be retained for "relayout." The emitted elements have their positions baked in (per PanelElement's "fixed at construction; never mutated" contract) and are added to a Panel like any other elements.

Helper, not container. Row does NOT implement PanelElement, does NOT have a render(...) method, and does NOT exist at runtime. The Panel renders the emitted elements directly with no indirection — preserving "Panel is the ceiling of composition" (THESIS).

Usage

List<PanelElement> buttonRow = Row.at(20, 30).spacing(4)
    .add(Button.spec(60, 20, Component.literal("OK"), this::onConfirm))
    .add(Button.spec(60, 20, Component.literal("Cancel"), this::onCancel))
    .build();

Panel p = Panel.builder("confirm")
    .elements(buttonRow).style(PanelStyle.RAISED).build();

Nesting

Row supports nesting via Row.Builder.addRow(Consumer) and Row.Builder.addColumn(Consumer). Nested helpers compose: each helper emits a flat list of positioned elements relative to its own origin; outer helpers translate the inner list by their computed child offset. After build(), the result is a flat list with all positions computed — no nested helper objects survive.

      public static Row.Builder at(int originX, int originY)
      Begin a row layout at the given panel-local origin.
      Parameters:
      originX - the panel-local X coordinate where the row's first child's left edge will be placed
      originY - the panel-local Y coordinate where the row sits (cross-axis alignment is applied within [originY, originY + maxChildHeight])
